Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

**Position Overview**
=====================

The Event Security Specialist will serve as the primary security professional responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing security operations for corporate events, executive engagements, leadership meetings, and other high-profile activities across Micron's global footprint.

The role is responsible for conducting event risk assessments, developing security plans, coordinating security resources, supporting executive protection requirements, managing incident response, and helping protect attendees, company assets, and sensitive information.

As a Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM) Subject Matter Expert, the individual will conduct and support technical security inspections of meeting venues, executive spaces, boardrooms, conference facilities, hotels, and other locations where sensitive discussions may occur. The role will deploy as required in support of executive events and strategic business activities.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**Event Security**
------------------

* Serve as the primary security lead for corporate events, executive engagements, and high-profile company functions.
* Conduct event security risk assessments and develop practical mitigation strategies.
* Develop comprehensive security plans, emergency response procedures, and operational security documentation.
* Coordinate with executive protection personnel, venue management, event organizers, law enforcement, and third-party security providers.
* Support site surveys, protective advances, route analysis, and venue assessments.

* Identify, assess, document, and mitigate potential technical surveillance vulnerabilities.
* Provide technical security recommendations designed to reduce the risk of unauthorized technical collection and eavesdropping.
* Prepare professional TSCM assessment reports, findings, and leadership briefings.

* Support secure movement planning and contingency operations for executive activities.

* Five or more years of experience in event security, executive protection, physical security, law enforcement, military, intelligence, or a comparable security environment.

* Demonstrated hands-on experience conducting TSCM inspections and using professional TSCM equipment and methodologies.

This is an early-career Research Assistant to support laboratory research examining interactions among microorganisms, carbon compounds, and plants. * Support plant research by performing routine experimental procedures and monitoring plant growth and phenotype.
  
* Prepare microbiological growth media, chemical stocks, and other laboratory materials, and perform routine DNA extractions.
  
* Conduct routine laboratory assays and accurately collect, record, organize, and maintain experimental data.
  
* Maintain microbial cultures, freezer stocks, and associated sample records and inventories.

* Familiarity with microbial sequence analysis or 16S rRNA gene analysis.
  
* Experience maintaining microbial culture collections or freezer stocks.
  
* Experience working with plants in laboratory or controlled-environment experiments.

jobs.description:
The Staff Research Associate (SRA) assists the principal investigator (PI) with active experiments and the daily tasks related to the operation of a biomedical research laboratory. This is a great opportunity for individuals interested in graduate school in the biomedical sciences.

Our research is primarily focused on: 1) chronic hypoxia sensing and adaptation, 2) mechanisms of pericarditis, and 3) lipid metabolism in hypoxia. We seek to understand how cells, tissues, and organisms respond and adapt to chronic hypoxia at the molecular and whole-body physiology levels. We utilize a variety of *in vitro* (cell) models and mouse models to investigate specific transcription factors, gene and protein regulatory pathways, and metabolic changes in mediating responses under hypoxia. This work lies at the intersection of hypoxia signaling, lipid metabolism, and cardiovascular disease. We have developed models of cardiovascular disease that are affected by chronic hypoxia, including pulmonary hypertension, heart failure, and obesity. We use various biochemical assays, “multi-omics,” and computational approaches to carefully dissect mechanisms of hypoxia adaptation and lipid rewiring in hypoxia. In addition, we are interested in dissecting mechanisms of recurrent pericarditis, using mouse models of pericarditis and patient samples.

The SRA will have many duties relevant to these goals and it is expected that they will become increasing independent over time. It is expected that the SRA will become well-versed in multiple molecular and biochemical techniques to analyze tissues and cells, such as western blotting, qPCR, single nuclear RNA sequencing, and generation of DNA constructs. They will also assist with various mouse model experiments and take an active role in mouse colony maintenance and lab organization and lab management.

  

Required Qualifications:

Responsibilities:

The Laboratory Assistant will follow the guidelines set by CLIA, and the California Business and Professions Code Sections 1212 and 1269. Unlicensed laboratory personnel (“aides”) are limited to pre-analytical and supportive functions only and may not read, record, result, verify, or interpret any laboratory test. They may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimens or reagents, conduct mathematical calculations related to test results, perform instrument calibration, or monitor or interpret quality control data used to assess test system performance. Unlicensed personnel shall not participate in any phase of testing that involves result generation, interpretation, verification, or reporting.

All duties must be performed under the direct and constant supervision of a physician and surgeon or a licensed laboratory professional, as defined by California regulations.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel may perform approved activities including specimen collection (patient preparation, labeling, handling, processing, preservation, transportation, and storage), assisting licensed personnel, preparing and storing reagents and culture media, assisting with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (without calibration or performance verification), and supporting quality control procedures (without interpretation of results). Specimen collection involving venipuncture or skin puncture may only be performed if the individual holds appropriate California phlebotomy certification (e.g., CPT I or CPT II) or other qualifying license, as required by law.

This individual: 1) Performs computer entry, filing, telephone communication, and other clerical duties. 2) Demonstrates professional telephone etiquette and greets patients and visitors courteously. 3) Possesses effective verbal and written communication skills. 4) Demonstrates knowledge of laboratory test terminology. 5) Demonstrates knowledge of phlebotomy practices; performs venipuncture or skin puncture only if appropriately certified per California law. 6) Processes specimens across laboratory departments including pathology, microbiology, immunology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, chemistry, and blood bank limited to pre-analytical activities (e.g., specimen handling and centrifugation only in immunohematology). 7) Prepares and processes specimens for reference laboratories. 8) Stocks and orders routine supplies. 9) Maintains cleanliness and organization of storage areas, equipment, centrifuges, and collection sites. 10) Processes and places specimens on laboratory instruments for automated analysis only, without performing test setup, calibration, validation, or result review. 11) With documented training, may assist with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (excluding calibration and performance verification), assist in quality control procedures (without interpreting results), and perform permitted microbiology support tasks such as primary culture inoculation, slide staining, and subculturing. 12) Performs additional duties assigned by department leadership, including clerical support, communication tasks, specimen transport, and interdepartmental deliveries. 13) Assists Pathology with pre-analytical and clerical tasks only, including specimen receipt, accessioning, labeling, transport, and storage, under direct supervision and within regulatory limitations. 14) Functions as a runner to support laboratory workflow and specimen movement as needed.

Responsibilities:

The Laboratory Assistant will follow the guidelines set by CLIA, and the California Business and Professions Code Sections 1212 and 1269. Unlicensed laboratory personnel (“aides”) are limited to pre-analytical and supportive functions only and may not read, record, result, verify, or interpret any laboratory test. They may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimens or reagents, conduct mathematical calculations related to test results, perform instrument calibration, or monitor or interpret quality control data used to assess test system performance. Unlicensed personnel shall not participate in any phase of testing that involves result generation, interpretation, verification, or reporting.

All duties must be performed under the direct and constant supervision of a physician and surgeon or a licensed laboratory professional, as defined by California regulations.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel may perform approved activities including specimen collection (patient preparation, labeling, handling, processing, preservation, transportation, and storage), assisting licensed personnel, preparing and storing reagents and culture media, assisting with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (without calibration or performance verification), and supporting quality control procedures (without interpretation of results). Specimen collection involving venipuncture or skin puncture may only be performed if the individual holds appropriate California phlebotomy certification (e.g., CPT I or CPT II) or other qualifying license, as required by law.

This individual: 1) Performs computer entry, filing, telephone communication, and other clerical duties. 2) Demonstrates professional telephone etiquette and greets patients and visitors courteously. 3) Possesses effective verbal and written communication skills. 4) Demonstrates knowledge of laboratory test terminology. 5) Demonstrates knowledge of phlebotomy practices; performs venipuncture or skin puncture only if appropriately certified per California law. 6) Processes specimens across laboratory departments including pathology, microbiology, immunology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, chemistry, and blood bank limited to pre-analytical activities (e.g., specimen handling and centrifugation only in immunohematology). 7) Prepares and processes specimens for reference laboratories. 8) Stocks and orders routine supplies. 9) Maintains cleanliness and organization of storage areas, equipment, centrifuges, and collection sites. 10) Processes and places specimens on laboratory instruments for automated analysis only, without performing test setup, calibration, validation, or result review. 11) With documented training, may assist with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (excluding calibration and performance verification), assist in quality control procedures (without interpreting results), and perform permitted microbiology support tasks such as primary culture inoculation, slide staining, and subculturing. 12) Performs additional duties assigned by department leadership, including clerical support, communication tasks, specimen transport, and interdepartmental deliveries. 13) Assists Pathology with pre-analytical and clerical tasks only, including specimen receipt, accessioning, labeling, transport, and storage, under direct supervision and within regulatory limitations. 14) Functions as a runner to support laboratory workflow and specimen movement as needed.

**About Shine Foods, Inc.**

Since 1996, Shine Foods has been making some of the most delicious and authentic Asian appetizers in the country. We take great pride in being a resource for private label manufacturing and co-packing needs. We work with our customers on creating new exclusive recipes, modifying and commercializing recipes for production. Today, we have grown to be one of the leading custom Asian appetizer manufacturers and co-packing companies serving local communities, retail and foodservice outlets across North America and beyond.

**Job Summary** We are seeking a diligent and detail-oriented QC (Quality Control) Technician to join our team. The QC Technician will be responsible for ensuring compliance with established quality standards and performing various quality control tests and inspections on products and materials. The ideal candidate should possess strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and a passion for maintaining high-quality standards in a production environment.

**Essential Job Functions**

* Monitor product formulations during ingredients, and filling preparation, document lot information (for traceability) of ingredients, raw materials, during processing, and documenting it on the Daily Product Mixing Batch Checking report.
* Monitor forming processing, product identity, weights, quality of product during the forming process, weight control, line condition, etc.
* Monitor internal temperature of product off the steamer, and document them on the CCP 1B Cooking Log. Make sure corrective actions are taken when deviations occur. Performs sensory evaluation of product off the steamer.
* Monitoring and documenting product temperature off the Spiral freezer, Product quality (shape, damaged, broken, deformed), weights, organoleptic properties of finish product, case counts, lot information, labeling, code dates, etc.
* Maintains and organize filing system for QA evaluation data.
* Environmental and allergen swabbing.
* Monitors and reviews recorded line QC and Production paper work for accuracy and completion.
* Check Metal detector, X-Ray machine, Weight checker, before packaging start.
* Routine random checks on finish products weight, temperature, and packaging date codes/lots during production at make-up lines and Re-packing.
* Inspects Metal detector/X-ray rejected products for foreign objects, and record findings.
* Monitors and audits CCP documentation, such as reviewing labeling, production, and performs random verification on Metal detector/X-Ray machine during production.
* Audits employee compliance, to GMP’s, SOP’s, and SSOP.
* Inspects incoming perishable ingredients.
* Interacts with Production to trouble-shoot quality issues.
* Conducts investigations into non-conforming materials and products.
* Performs other duties as required or directed by QA Manager.

**Food Safety Responsibilities**

* All employees are required to immediately report and assist in the elimination or control of any food safety issues they observe to their supervisor
* Monitors and enforces cGMPs
* Follow all Good Manufacturing Practices and Pre-requisite programs

**Qualifications:**

* High school diploma or equivalent
* Minimum of 6 months experience in QC or QA
* Strong knowledge of quality control best practices, test procedures, and applicable standards and regulations
* Proficient in using various quality control tools and equipment
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with a keen eye for detail.
* Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
* Computer literacy: Proficient

**Physical Requirement:**

* Ability to occasionally lift 35-50Ibs
* Ability to stand and sit for prolong periods
* Ability to walk through production areas
* Exposure to temperature change
* Wear proper footwear
* Vision abilities include close, distance, peripheral, and depth perception

**Schedule:**

* 2nd shift (3 p.m. - 11:30 p.m.)

S**upervisor:** QA Manager

**Job Type**: Full-time

 **The pay range for this role is:**  
19 - 20 USD per hour(Torrance)
